record.original_question: Let M be a connected Riemannian manifold isometrically immersed in Euclidean (n+1)-space E^(n+1). The immersion is of finite type when its position vector can be written as a finite sum x = c + x1 + ... + xk of E^(n+1)-valued Laplace eigenmaps satisfying Delta xi = lambda_i xi. Classify all finite type hypersurfaces in E^(n+1); in particular, classify all finite type surfaces in E^3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a connected Riemannian manifold and let $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ be an isometric immersion into Euclidean $(n+1)$-space. Identify $x$ with the position vector field of $M$ in $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced metric on $M$, acting componentwise on $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$-valued functions. The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type if there exist a constant vector $c \in \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$, a positive integer $k$, real numbers $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k$, and non-constant $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$-valued maps $x_1, \dots, x_k$ on $M$ such that
$$x = c + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k, \qquad \Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i \;\;\text{for } i=1,\dots,k.$$
Problem: Classify, up to congruence, all finite type hypersurfaces $M^n \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$. In particular, classify all finite type surfaces in $\mathbb{E}^3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of finite type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space, and even of finite type surfaces in E^3, is a long-standing open problem of B.-Y. Chen. The only known finite type surfaces in E^3 are open pieces of spheres, circular cylinders, and minimal surfaces; whether others exist remains unresolved, and recent works (2015–2025) continue to address only special subclasses (ruled, factorable, Gauss-map finite type, etc.).

status_evidence.title: On Surfaces of finite Chen-type — Stamatakis & Al-Zoubi
status_evidence.snippet: The only known finite Chen-type surfaces in E^3 are portions of spheres, circular cylinders and minimal surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond these three families, the classification problem in E^3 is still open.

status_evidence.title: On surfaces of finite type in Euclidean 3-space (Kodai Math. J.)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies finite type surfaces in E^3 and addresses partial classification results.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results toward Chen's classification problem are available.
